title: With-or-without-you: the average swing is basically zero
headline_insight: Across 408 qualified players, a team's win rate with the player active versus missing swings by only +0.0087 on average -- the extremes are loud (Brandon Miller: Charlotte 63.1% with him, 17.6% without) but small-sample and confounded.
what_it_means: This is a RAPM-free proxy for player impact: compare a team's win rate in the games a player played versus sat, inside his own tenure window. The average delta sitting near zero is the honest takeaway -- most 'the team is lost without him' stories don't survive when you actually split the games. The eye-popping individual numbers ride on a handful of missed games and everything a raw with/without ignores: which other stars were also out, whether the sit-games were blowout rests, who replaced him.
how_to_read: delta_win_rate is win-rate-active minus win-rate-missed; each entry carries a Wald 95% CI offset that is wide for players with few missed games.
why_it_matters: It shows why the platform treats on/off and with/without as descriptive context, not a plug-and-play player value -- the signal is real but drowned in roster confounds until an earned predictive receipt says otherwise.
caveat: WITH/WITHOUT = ROSTER CONFOUND: why a player missed games is entangled with injury clustering, rest scheduling, blowout pulls, and a different replacement lineup, none controlled for. DESCRIPTIVE_ONLY, not a predictive or edge claim.
